text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 1.12 runtime rollout with fused-attn kernels we pushed ~03:10 UTC, we've got a significant drop in prompt warmup hits on rw-instruct-v2-7b-quant. p95 latency up ~8%, token-costs up, and warmup hit-rate fell from ~86% -> ~42% on short prompts (<=64 tokens). Repro + quick logs below. :frowning:

sanjay: Which fleet/region? Dedicated or hosted?

maria: hosted-us-east, default pool (fw:rw-7b-quant). Deploy id: deploy-bot/2026-03-18-0310 (see deploy-bot msg). Seen across small-batch traffic (batch_size 1-4). Works fine for long prompts (>=512), only short prompt workloads hit it hard.

maria: Repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-v2-7b-quant","input":"hello","max_tokens":32}' -v
# check response headers: x-prefix-warmup: miss/hit
```
We instrumented a header `x-prefix-warmup` in runtime; many requests show `miss`.

perf-bot: ALERT: prefix_warmup_hit_rate drop > 30% on rw-instruct-v2-7b-quant (hosted-us-east) between 03:08-03:20 UTC. Triggered at 03:22 UTC. See perf dashboard: https://perf/redwood/alerts/4729 :eyes:

aisha: I sampled the KV fingerprints from trace logs for a few requests (before vs after). Pre-rollout: kv_fp=0x9ac3e7f2... Post-rollout: kv_fp=0x4da7b11c... Same prompt/tokenization -> different fp. Looks like the fused-attn path serializes/normalizes KV cache differently (ordering + trailing-zero trimming).

sanjay: That explains misses. Did we change any key canonicalization in compile? IIRC we only changed kernel selection but compiler also touched attention packing.

maria: No explicit canonicalization change in code, but compiler/encoder in 1.12 adds an attention-slab packing step for fused-attn which alters buffer layout. The runtime keying uses raw bytes of KV tensors hashed via xxh3. If layout changes, fingerprint changes.

ryan: Quick test: toggled runtime flag `ATTN_KERNEL=unfused` on a small canary host. Warmup hit-rate returned to ~84% within 10 minutes for same traffic. So this is definitely layout/key mismatch, not tokenizer.

aisha: Profiling snippets (sanitized):
```
# pre-1.12 (unfused)
kv_bytes = [len=8192, layout=row-major, trailing zeros kept]
hash(xxhash(kv_bytes)) -> 0x9ac3e7f2
# post-1.12 (fused)
kv_bytes = [len=8064, layout=packed-slab, trailing zeros trimmed]
hash(xxhash(kv_bytes)) -> 0x4da7b11c
```

sanjay: Two immediate mitigation options:
1) Canonicalize KV before hashing (serialize to canonical format: dims + flattened float16 LE, pad deterministic) — safe but CPU cost.
2) Revert fused-attn kernel for 7b-quant until we fix canonicalization — quick and lower-risk.

maria: +1 to revert for hosted pools. We need an acceptably fast canonicalization in runtime for Dedicated later.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-18-0309 -> rolled to hosted-us-east (1.12). Rollback PR prepared: https://git/reverts/rollout-1.12-7b-quant

ryan: I can push rollback to canary now and staged hosts in us-east. If canary looks good for 30m we can roll global.

aisha: I'll open a short-lived ticket with profiling artifacts and propose canonical serialization format: include shape, dtype, and fixed little-endian ordering, pad to 8-byte boundary. Add unit test to ensure identical hash across kernels.

maria: Action items:
- ryan: roll canary rollback -> now. (owner)
- aisha: spec canonical serialization + test -> PR today. (owner)
- sanjay: add a hot-fix CPU-path canonicalizer opt-in flag with low overhead; benchmark. (owner)
- oncall: watch perf dashboard -> tag me if regression persists. @oncall :bell:

sanjay: also add a short note in release docs: kernel changes can change binary layout; warn model teams about potential cache invalidation.

maria: Thanks. Will update the incident ticket with perf numbers and ETA. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: NOTE: Warmup hit-rate currently at 78% on canary after rollback test (03:45 UTC). Monitoring.

maria: Closing loop: if warmup hit-rate stays >80% for 1h we mark rollback successful and schedule a patch release for canonicalization. If not, we'll keep rollback and escalate.

ryan: Canary rolled back at 03:36 UTC. Will post timeline and logs in the ticket.

maria: FYI saved repro traces to s3://redwood-debug/prefix-warmup/2005001234/ for folks who want raw logs.

sanjay: Good catch. Learned: kernel runtime changes -> possible KV fingerprint drift. We should add a raft of unit/integration tests to catch this earlier (hash invariants across kernel choices).
